summary: Specifies the data export format for version 9 of Cisco's NetFlow services, used by network elements and matching collectors. It uses templates, which describe collections of fields, to make observations of IP packet flows flexible and extensible.

plainLanguage.summary: NetFlow version 9 sends traffic records with templates that describe their fields. A collector uses those templates to interpret data and can receive new fields without changing the overall packet format.

questions: how does netflow version 9 differ from earlier versions
subtitle: A template-based export format for sending IP flow records from network devices to collectors.

tldr.problem: Network devices collect information about IP flows, but a fixed record format makes it difficult to add or select fields without changing the format.
tldr.mechanism: NetFlow version 9 sends templates that define fields and lengths, followed by data records that use those templates. An export packet contains a header and one or more FlowSets.
tldr.outcome: Templates make the export format extensible and let collectors interpret record structure even if they do not understand every field's meaning. NetFlow version 9 was submitted as a basis for IPFIX work.

today: RFC 3954 is an Informational RFC published in October 2004, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It documents NetFlow version 9 as submitted to the IETF as a basis for IPFIX work.

sections.title: Flow Records and Templates
sections.content:
A flow is a unidirectional sequence of packets with common properties observed at a network device. An exporter gathers flow information and sends Flow Records to a collector. Records may include addresses, packet and byte counts, timestamps, service information, ports, and interfaces.

NetFlow version 9 uses templates to define collections of fields and their structure. This lets exporters add fields without changing the export record format, and lets them send only the fields needed. A collector can interpret record structure even when it does not understand the meaning of every field.
sections.plainLanguage: A network device records information about groups of related packets and sends the records to a collector. A template describes the fields in those records.

sections.title: Exporters, Collectors and FlowSets
sections.content:
An Exporter creates flows from observed packets, and a NetFlow Collector receives and processes Flow Records. An Export Packet consists of a Packet Header followed by one or more FlowSets. A FlowSet groups records with a similar structure.

The three FlowSet types are Template FlowSets, Options Template FlowSets, and Data FlowSets. Template FlowSets describe flow-data records. Options templates describe records about the NetFlow process, such as a sampling rate. Data FlowSets contain values described by a previously sent template. Binary integers MUST use network byte order.
sections.plainLanguage: The exporter sends packets to a collector. Each packet begins with a header and then carries templates, flow data, or information about the exporter itself.

sections.title: The Export Packet Header
sections.content:
The header fields are Version, Count, sysUpTime, UNIX seconds, Sequence Number, and Source ID. Version is 9. Count is the total number of records in the packet, including Options, Template, and Data FlowSet records.

sysUpTime measures milliseconds since the device first booted. UNIX seconds records the time the packet leaves the Exporter. Sequence Number is a cumulative counter for packets from an Observation Domain and SHOULD help a Collector identify missed packets. Source ID identifies the Exporter Observation Domain.
sections.plainLanguage: The header identifies the format and the observation domain, counts records, and records timing and sequence information. A collector can use the sequence number to notice that export packets may have been missed.

sections.title: Template, Data and Options Records
sections.content:
A Template FlowSet has ID 0 and contains Template Records. Each record has a Template ID, a field count, and a type and length for each field. Template IDs used for data start at 256; values from 0 through 255 are reserved. A Data FlowSet uses the corresponding Template ID as its FlowSet ID, and its values follow the field order and lengths in that template.

Options templates describe information about the exporter or NetFlow process, rather than IP flows. Their FlowSet ID is 1 and their scope identifies where the options apply, such as a system, interface, line card, cache, or template. Data FlowSets can include padding to align the next FlowSet on a 4-byte boundary.
sections.plainLanguage: A template tells the collector how to read fields in later data records. Options templates describe the scope of information about the exporter rather than the observed flows.

sections.title: Template Management and Security
sections.content:
Because templates do not appear in every packet, a Collector MUST keep them to interpret later data. Template IDs are local to an Observation Domain and may change when an Exporter or NetFlow process restarts. Exporters MUST send templates before data that depends on them and MUST resend templates regularly so the Collector can refresh them.

The RFC describes NetFlow version 9 as designed for Exporters and Collectors in a single private network. It does not provide confidentiality, integrity, or authentication. If export packets are exposed to the public Internet, they could be captured, modified, or forged; forged templates could also prevent a Collector from decoding records. The RFC notes that IPFIX work based on version 9 addresses these security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The collector needs current templates before it can interpret data. Export packets are not protected by this protocol, so an attacker who can reach them may read or forge the records.

fields.name: Count
fields.desc: Total number of records in the Export Packet.

fields.name: sysUpTime
fields.desc: Milliseconds since the device first booted.

fields.name: UNIX Secs
fields.desc: Time in seconds when the packet leaves the Exporter.

fields.name: Sequence Number
fields.desc: Cumulative Export Packet counter for the Observation Domain.
